translation:
Although [the person] drinks much, the water fluids ultimately cannot moisten beyond the intestines and stomach; the thirst does not stop and the stool pours out, becoming copious urination.

The vulgar physicians of this declining age, not understanding this, recklessly say it is deficiency-cold of the lower burner, and many are wrongly killed. Again, as with wind-heat and dryness-depression throughout the body, it may become eye obstruction (目瘴), carbuncles and deep abscesses (癰疽), and sores and ulcers (瘡瘍); above it becomes panting and cough, and below it becomes atrophy and bi (痿痹).
translator_notes: 叔世俗流 rendered as 'the vulgar physicians of this declining age'.
痿痹 rendered as 'atrophy and bi'.
